intro: Every town has places to play. Some are parks. Some are school gyms. Some are fields with tall lights. People in the town paid for them together.
Games need rules too. Some rules are painted lines. Some are printed in books. In 1863, clubs in London wrote rules for football. In 1900, Illinois high schools began the IHSA.
In this unit, you will meet real places and real rule books. You will learn who paid for them and who wrote them. You will see how they help strangers play together.
bigQuestion: Who builds the places where a town plays, and who writes the rules everyone shares?

timeline.t: Clubs meet in London and form the Football Association

IFAB forms to keep soccer's rule book
James Naismith's class plays basketball in a Springfield gym
The Triangle prints Naismith's thirteen rules
Electric lights fill Chicago's world's fair at night
Illinois high schools form the IHSA
Chicago's South Side opens small parks with field houses
First IHSA boys wrestling state champions
Lights go up at Wrigley Field
First IHSA girls wrestling state finals
